summary:
The gate stamp is carefully built. The parser handles the three known gate shapes, the hash errs toward firing, stamping is idempotent and keeps the executable bit, and the harness pins the fixture hashes and checks this checkout's own stamp.

The findings sit at the edges of that design:
- **Self-hosted rules:** they miss a fix that changes the hash definition, and the new `defer` for checks.sh contradicts the shaper's rule 7.
- **Section choice:** the gate can switch silently to the plan-template decoy.
- **Allow list:** the shared rule pre-approves `stamp` as well as `check`.
- **Smaller mismatches:** a few lines of documentation, one argument path and one test helper disagree with what the code does.

An earlier launch wrote a round-1 record for this PR (agent-os/specs/2026-10-21-1359-7-review-round-1/redline/, committed in 6adcf2b). Its review never reached the PR: `has-review` finds none, and the PR has no comments. Its seven findings were checked again and keep their IDs, R1-1 to R1-7; R1-8 to R1-10 are new.

Concurrency: this repository has no scheduled commands or queued jobs. Only a hand-run `stamp` writes checks.sh, in place, at a point where a launch has already refused. The precheck and the gate test only read it.

findings.title: Point 11 does not defer a fix that changes how this checkout's hash is computed
findings.description:
Point 11, and the matching Known limits line at README.md:147, send only one kind of finding to `defer`: one whose fix changes the gate's backticked text. A second kind also needs a restamp. That is a fix in scripts/redline-gate.sh that changes the hash definition (the normalisation, the join, what counts as an item) or the stamp line's format. Either one invalidates this checkout's stamp.

Here the guard lets the implementer edit scripts/redline-gate.sh (tests/guard-cases.tsv, `allow Edit scripts/redline-gate.sh` under `# @cwd PLUGIN`) but refuses `.claude/redline/` to every role. So the implementer can repin the fixture hashes in tests/gate-test.sh but cannot restamp. The harness's last case (`check "$PLUGIN"`) then stays red and the `gate` check in checks.sh fails. The implementer can only return `blocked`, which workflows/redline-loop.js:1351-1352 turns into a stage error, and the round ends with nothing pushed.

A shaper following point 11 as written sorts such a finding as an ordinary `fix`. Option (c) of R1-6 is one.
findings.proposedFix: Extend point 11 and the Known limits line. A finding whose fix changes how scripts/redline-gate.sh computes the hash, or how it formats the stamp line, also needs a restamp, so it is `defer` and a person restamps after the run. Point 11 sits outside the gate section, so this edit does not move the hash. If gate step 6's sentence is extended too, keep the new words outside backticks for the same reason.

findings.title: Point 11's checks.sh `defer` contradicts the shaper's overriding rule 7
findings.description:
Point 11 now says "The same holds for `.claude/redline/checks.sh`", which makes a finding there `defer`. Rule 7 of agents/redline-shaper.md (line 25) sits under "Rules that override everything else". It says a finding on `.claude/redline/` is never `fix` or `defer` but `ask`, and its self-hosted exception names only scripts/redline-guard.sh and hooks/hooks.json. A shaper reading both gets opposite dispositions for a checks.sh finding, and the overriding rule wins.

When point 11 first gained the guard and the hook, PR #5 round 1 added a matching exception to rule 7 (agent-os/specs/2026-10-21-1108-5-review-round-1/shape.md, Decisions, R1-1). This change does not add one for checks.sh.
findings.proposedFix: Add `.claude/redline/checks.sh` to the self-hosted exception in agents/redline-shaper.md rule 7. A finding there, or one whose fix changes the gate's backticked text, is `defer`, as the repository's unattended-mode section says.

findings.title: Gate step 6 still says about 20 seconds; checks.sh records 29
findings.description: This change rewrites the continuation line under gate step 6 ("Steps 1 to 6 are what ..."), but the line still ends "About 20 seconds on 2026-10-21". For the same six checks, the header of .claude/redline/checks.sh (line 24) records "Baseline on 2026-10-21: 29 seconds". agent-os/standards/testing/tests.md names that header as the place the baseline time is kept.
findings.proposedFix: Change the sentence to match the header (about 30 seconds), or drop it and point to the header. The words are prose outside backticks, so the hash does not move and no restamp is needed.

findings.title: Upgrading says "stamped once", but each older PR branch is refused too
findings.description: The Upgrading section says a repository is stamped once and that this is the whole upgrade. But the precheck reads checks.sh from the PR's head: items 3 to 5 of skills/redline/SKILL.md section 4 require HEAD to be the PR branch at its pushed head with a clean tree. So a PR branch cut before the stamp commit reached its base carries no stamp, and its launch stops with "carries no gate stamp". Stamping on that branch dirties the tree (item 4) and needs a commit pushed to the PR (item 5), unless the base is merged in instead. The section does not say so.
findings.proposedFix: Add one sentence to Upgrading. A PR branch cut before the stamp commit carries no stamp: merge its base into it, or stamp it on the branch and commit and push, before launching on it.

findings.title: Template says to restamp "with the command in the TODO line", which stamping removes
findings.description: The template header tells the reader to "restamp it with the command in the TODO line". But `stamp` replaces that TODO line with the stamp itself. A restamp is only ever needed in a checks.sh that is already stamped, and there the sentence points at a line that no longer exists. This repository's own checks.sh writes the command out instead (.claude/redline/checks.sh line 39).
findings.proposedFix: Write the command into the sentence, as this repository's checks.sh does: "restamp it: <plugin>/scripts/redline-gate.sh stamp .claude/commands/agent-os/shape-spec.md .claude/redline/checks.sh".

findings.title: Gate selection can switch silently to the plan-template decoy
findings.description:
Pass 2 takes the first heading containing "verification gate" whose section holds a `1.` line. Headings inside a column-0 fence count, because Losers League's gate sits in one. In this repository the plan template's `## Task N: Verification Gate` (shape-spec.md line 202, inside the fence that runs from 179 to 209) comes before the real `## Verification Gate` at line 234. Chalkboard's file has the same layout. Today the decoy is skipped only because it holds no numbered list.

If that template task is ever written as a numbered list, which is the form Losers League's fixture already uses, `extract` picks the decoy. `check` fails once with "gate changed", and the person restamps as the line tells them. Neither `stamp`'s output nor `check`'s stderr line names the heading or line that was hashed, and the skill shows only the stderr line. From then on, edits to the real gate never move the hash: the false negative the stamp exists to prevent, and nothing makes it visible. The fixtures cover only decoys written in prose.

Question for the person: when two sections qualify, should the script choose one, refuse, or say which one it used?
findings.proposedFix:
Options for the person:
(a) When more than one "verification gate" section holds a numbered list, exit 1 and name both lines, so a person picks; a `--heading-line` flag on `stamp` could record the choice.
(b) Prefer a section outside any fence over one inside a fence.
(c) Have `stamp` print the chosen heading and line on stderr, and/or record the heading line in the stamp. Recording it changes the stamp format, which needs a person to restamp this checkout (R1-1).
Each option needs a fixture with two sections that both hold a numbered list.

findings.title: `stamp ... --steps` with no value exits 1 silently
findings.description: `--steps) range="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;`: when `--steps` is the last argument (`stamp shape-spec.md checks.sh --steps`), `shift 2` runs with one positional parameter left. It fails without shifting, and under `set -euo pipefail` the script exits 1 with no message. The header (lines 32-33) and the README table document exit 1 as "the file has no gate" and exit 2 as "a bad or missing --steps".
findings.proposedFix: `--steps) [[ $# -ge 2 ]] || usage; range="$2"; shift 2 ;;`, plus a gate-test case: `expect_exit "--steps with no value: exit 2" 2 stamp "$SPEC" --steps`.

findings.title: Precheck item 1 says "stop as step 1 does", but item 1 is now the gate check itself
findings.description: The gate check is now item 1 of section 4, and the other items are renumbered. Its exit-2 sentence says "stop as step 1 does: this repository is not set up for Redline yet", meaning section 1 (Resolve the repository). The unchanged line 79 also says the working directory is one "which step 1 established is inside the checkout", again meaning section 1. Read inside section 4, "step 1" now names the gate check, so both references point the agent following them at the wrong step.
findings.proposedFix: Say "section 1" in both places, for example "stop as section 1 does" and "which section 1 established is inside the checkout".

findings.title: The allow rule pre-approves `stamp`, the step reserved for a person
findings.description:
`Bash(/*/scripts/redline-gate.sh *)` pre-approves every subcommand, `stamp` included, for any session outside a Redline role, where the guard is inert. The same rule is at .claude/settings.json:7. The plan's stated purpose (Task 4) is only that the precheck's `check` never prompts.

But stamping is the step the design leaves to a person: SKILL.md section 4 says "never stamp or edit `checks.sh`: a person does that", and `check`'s own failure line prints the full stamp command. A main-session agent asked to get a refused launch going can run that command with no permission prompt. That restamps without bringing checks.sh up to date, which approves the very drift the stamp exists to catch. The existing script rules (redline-gh.sh, redline-prefs.sh) also allow every subcommand, so a rule per subcommand would be a new pattern here.

Question for the person: should `stamp` stay pre-approved, or should it always ask?
findings.proposedFix: Option 1: narrow both rules to `Bash(/*/scripts/redline-gate.sh check *)`. The precheck still never prompts, and a stamp always asks the person; /redline:setup can add its own rule when it lands. Option 2: keep the blanket rule and accept that the skill's prose is the only thing stopping the main session from stamping.

findings.title: `differs` passes when the mutated copy fails to parse
findings.description:
`differs` passes whenever the two `sha` outputs differ, and that includes an empty one. `sha` sends stderr to /dev/null, so when `extract` exits 1 or Python prints a traceback, it outputs nothing, and a fixture's pinned hash never equals an empty string.

The four cases at lines 137, 139, 141 and 143 (a sub-bullet span, the continuation span, a fenced command line, a nested span) have no follow-up assertion on the mutated file. So a parser crash on exactly the construct a case mutates would be reported as a pass. The standard this PR adds to agent-os/standards/testing/tests.md covers only the case where both outputs are empty.
findings.proposedFix: Make `differs` require a real hash on the mutated side: `differs() { local a b; a="$(sha "$WORK/$2")"; b="$(sha "$WORK/$3")"; [[ "$b" =~ ^[0-9a-f]{64}$ && "$a" != "$b" ]] && ok "$1" || bad "$1" "$a vs $b"; }`.
